seo_luxury.title: Luxury homestay and boutique stay in Udaipur that feels like home
seo_luxury.body:
Looking for a **luxury homestay in Udaipur** that feels like a private country home rather than a hotel? Devra is a boutique homestay set on a small hillock in a green estate of five acres, only 10–15 minutes from Udaipur city centre. It has eight spacious rooms, an infinity pool with a view of the city line, courtyards with lily ponds and a 360-degree view of the Aravalli hills, the Sajjan Garh fort and an 800-year-old temple.

Devra is hosted by Major Durga Das (ex-Indian Army) and Jyoti Jasol, who live on the property and look after every guest personally. In the local language, ‘Devra’ means ‘a tribal temple where God resides’.

![Devra and its green estate](media:m-landscape)

## A boutique homestay, not a hotel

With only eight rooms, Devra is small by design. There is no lobby crowd and no buffet queue: meals are cooked for you, the hosts know you by name, and every corner of the estate is yours to explore. It is the reason guests describe it as one of the best homestays in Udaipur for a quiet, personal stay.

- Eight rooms only, so every stay gets personal attention
- Hosts who live on the property and know Udaipur well
- Farm-to-plate Rajasthani food, cooked to your taste
- Handpicked art, block-printed linen and traditional furniture
- Five acres of gardens, courtyards and farmland to wander

## Premium homestay comforts

Devra pairs rustic, heritage-rich décor with the comforts you expect from a **premium homestay in Udaipur**:

- Infinity pool with a view of the Udaipur city line
- Spacious, soundproof air-conditioned rooms: 6 double-bed and 2 twin-bed rooms
- Attached bathrooms with amenities and 24x7 running hot water
- Free Wi-Fi, so you can take a staycation and keep working
- Yoga, mehendi, laundry, taxis and auto rickshaws on request
- Airport and railway station pickup and drop on prior booking

![Four-poster room](media:w-08)

## Rooms with handpicked art and big bay windows

The rooms are spacious and soundproof, six with a double bed and two with twin beds, some with a bay-window day bed, a writing desk and space for an extra bed. Large bay windows bring in fresh air and sunlight, and the common spaces on every floor are open on three sides, so you feel the outdoors even when you are inside.

## Home-cooked Rajasthani food, from farm to plate

Food is one of the main reasons guests come back. Meals are prepared in traditional Rajasthani style with organic vegetables from Devra’s own farms, supervised by Jyoti Jasol herself. North Indian dishes are always available, and food can be customised to your taste, from children’s favourites to special diets.

![Cooking the traditional way](media:x-01)

## Things to do at Devra

- Birdwatching with Major Durga Das
- Heritage cooking demonstrations with Jyoti Jasol
- Yoga and meditation on the terrace, with the Aravalli hills all around
- Morning farm walks and bicycle tours to nearby villages
- Evenings of Rajasthani culture with the hosts

## A pet-friendly homestay in Udaipur

Travelling with your dog? Devra is a **pet-friendly homestay in Udaipur**, and your pet will find company with the pets of Devra on the open land. It is equally loved by couples, families, groups of friends, solo women travellers, artists and anyone looking for a staycation in nature.

## A luxury stay in Udaipur, 10 minutes from the lakes

A **luxury stay in Udaipur** usually means choosing between a large lake-view hotel in the crowded old city and a resort far outside it. Devra sits in between: close enough to reach Lake Pichola, the City Palace and the old-city bazaars in 10–15 minutes, and high enough on its hillock to wake up to birdsong, open farmland and the Aravalli hills. Spacious rooms, an infinity pool, home-cooked meals and hosts who plan your days with you make it a luxury stay without the formality of a hotel.

## A boutique stay in Udaipur for couples, families and friends

If you are looking for a **boutique stay in Udaipur**, Devra is built around small numbers and personal attention. Couples come for quiet mornings on the terrace and sunset dinners; families come for the space, the pool and the farm walks; groups of friends book the whole house for celebrations and get-togethers. With only eight rooms, every stay feels private.

## Why choose a luxury boutique homestay in Udaipur over a hotel?

- **Space:** five acres of gardens, courtyards and farmland instead of a corridor of rooms
- **People:** hosts who live on the property, not a rotating front desk
- **Food:** home-cooked Rajasthani meals from our own farm produce, not a buffet
- **Character:** handpicked art, block-printed linen and traditional furniture in every room
- **Calm:** birdsong, starry skies and views of the Aravalli hills, 10–15 minutes from the city

## Luxury, boutique or premium homestay: what is the difference?

A **luxury homestay** gives you the comfort of a good hotel (air-conditioned rooms, a pool, Wi-Fi, laundry and transfers) in a private home. A **boutique homestay** adds character: a small number of rooms, a house with a story, and decor chosen piece by piece. A **premium homestay** promises space and attention to detail. Devra is all three: eight rooms in a heritage-style home on five acres, hosted by the family who built it.

## A three-day Udaipur itinerary from Devra

**Day 1: Arrive and slow down.** Settle into your room, take a dip in the infinity pool and watch the sun set over the Aravalli hills from the terrace, followed by a home-cooked Rajasthani dinner.

**Day 2: The old city.** Spend the morning at the City Palace and Jagdish Temple, walk the lanes to Bagore ki Haveli for its evening cultural show, and end the day with a sunset boat ride on Lake Pichola.

**Day 3: Birds, food and forts.** Start with birdwatching or a farm walk with the hosts, join a heritage cooking demonstration, then visit Fateh Sagar Lake and the Sajjangarh (Monsoon) Palace at sunset. With an extra day, drive to Eklingji Temple (22 km) or Kumbhalgarh Fort and wildlife sanctuary (82 km), whose 36 km wall is the longest in India.

## How to reach our homestay in Udaipur

Udaipur is well connected by air, rail and road, and Devra can arrange pickup from the airport or the railway station on prior booking.

### From Delhi and the NCR

Direct flights from Delhi to Udaipur’s Maharana Pratap Airport take about an hour and a half. By rail, overnight trains such as the Mewar Express run from Delhi to Udaipur City station, and by road Udaipur is roughly 660 km from Delhi. Many guests from Delhi, Gurugram and Noida fly in for a long weekend.

### From Mumbai and Pune

Mumbai has direct flights to Udaipur, which makes Devra an easy luxury escape from Mumbai and Pune for a long weekend.

### From Ahmedabad and Gujarat

Udaipur is about 260 km from Ahmedabad, around four to five hours by road, so a drive to our boutique homestay is one of the most popular weekend getaways from Ahmedabad, Vadodara and the rest of Gujarat.

### From Jaipur and the rest of Rajasthan

Udaipur is about 400 km from Jaipur by road, with direct trains between the two cities. Devra fits easily into a Rajasthan circuit with Jaipur, Jodhpur, Chittorgarh and Kumbhalgarh.

### From Bengaluru, Hyderabad, Chennai and abroad

Fly to Udaipur directly where available, or connect through Delhi or Mumbai. International guests usually connect through Delhi or Mumbai.

## Close to the lakes, away from the noise

Devra is a 7-minute drive from Udaipur city centre, about 11 km from the bus station, 12 km from Udaipur railway station and 32 km from the airport. Lake Pichola, the City Palace, Jagdish Temple, Fateh Sagar Lake and the Sajjangarh (Monsoon) Palace are all within easy reach, and you return each evening to birdsong and starry skies on the hillock.

## Book your luxury homestay in Udaipur

Book directly with us online or send us a message on WhatsApp. Tell us your dates, how many of you are coming and anything you are celebrating, and we will take care of the rest.

posts.title: A photo walk through Devra
posts.excerpt: From the garden to the rooms, the lounges and the kitchen: a walk through Devra in pictures.
posts.body:
Devra sits on a small hillock in a green estate of five acres, 10–15 minutes from Udaipur city centre. A short walk through the house, in pictures.

![Devra and its green estate](media:m-landscape)

## The estate

Farmland all around, the Aravalli hills on the horizon and an infinity pool looking out over the city line.

![Plunge pool with a view of the hills](media:n-pool)

## Courtyards and gardens

Every level has a courtyard or a garden corner. On fine mornings, breakfast is laid out in the garden.

![Breakfast in the garden](media:w-44)

## Lounges for slow days

Lounges open on three sides, with handpicked art, deep sofas and old wooden furniture.

![Lounge with a painted mural](media:w-18)

## The rooms

Eight rooms: six with a double bed and two with twin beds. Some have four-poster beds, some a bay-window day bed.

![Four-poster room](media:w-08)

## The kitchen

Food is cooked the traditional Rajasthani way, with vegetables from our own farm.

![Cooking the traditional way](media:x-01)

We look forward to hosting you.

posts.title: A slow morning at Devra
posts.author: Team Devra
posts.excerpt: Birdsong, warm light and a walk through the farms: how a typical day begins on the hillock.
posts.body:
A typical day at Devra starts with chirping birds and mellow, warm sunlight knocking at your door. Take your morning tea or coffee outside, where the fresh air comes straight off the fields and the Aravalli hills sit on the horizon.

## Walk the farms with your hosts

Major Durga Das and Jyoti Jasol love to join guests on their morning walks through the farms. If you are travelling with a pet, it will find company with the pets of Devra while you watch them play in the open land.

## Birds, yoga and quiet corners

Major is a keen bird watcher and will gladly take you out for a birdwatching session. Prefer something slower? Yoga and meditation on the terrace are a favourite with guests, and there are plenty of nooks to read, paint or simply sit.

> Devra translates to *a tribal temple where God resides*.

When you are ready for the city, Udaipur's centre is only 10 to 15 minutes away.

posts.title: From our farm to your plate
posts.author: Team Devra
posts.excerpt: Organic vegetables from our own fields, spices processed on the property and recipes Jyoti grew up with.
posts.body:
Food is one of the reasons guests come back to Devra. Most vegetables come from our own farms and are grown free of toxic chemicals, and many of the spices are processed by locals right here on the property.

![The dining hall at Devra](media:w-59)

## Authentic Rajasthani cuisine

Every meal is cooked in traditional Rajasthani style and supervised by Jyoti Jasol herself. She learnt these recipes growing up in a large joint family and loves sharing the stories behind each dish.

## Something for everyone

Alongside Rajasthani food, the kitchen makes a variety of North Indian dishes and can adjust any meal to your taste. Pasta, noodles and sandwiches are available on request.

## Cook with Jyoti

Jyoti conducts heritage cooking classes on appointment. Ask us when you book and we will plan a session during your stay.

posts.title: Day trips from Devra: lakes, palaces and forts
posts.author: Team Devra
posts.excerpt: Udaipur's lakes and palaces are minutes away. Here is how we suggest planning your days.
posts.body:
Devra is 10 to 15 minutes from the city centre, so you can spend the day exploring and come back to the quiet of the hills by evening.

## In the city

- **Lake Pichola**: take the sunset boat ride.
- **City Palace**: massive courtyards and elaborate paintings on the bank of Lake Pichola.
- **Fateh Sagar Lake**: a calm lake with boat rides.
- **Bagore ki Haveli**: cultural shows with local performing artists.

## Further out

- **Eklingji Temple**, 22 km from Udaipur, known for its religious and cultural significance.
- **Kumbhalgarh**, 82 km away. The fort's 36 km wall is the longest in India and the second longest in the world after the Great Wall of China. There is a wildlife sanctuary too, and it is popular with trekkers.

## Getting around

We arrange taxis, and airport and railway station pickups on prior booking. Udaipur Airport is 32 km away and the railway station is 12 km.

faqs.q: Is Devra a luxury homestay or a hotel?
faqs.a: Devra is a boutique, family-run luxury homestay with eight rooms on a five-acre hillock estate in Udaipur. The hosts live on the property, so you get the comfort of a premium stay with the warmth of a home.

faqs.q: What makes Devra a luxury stay in Udaipur?
faqs.a: Spacious soundproof rooms, an infinity pool with a city-line view, home-cooked Rajasthani food, five acres of gardens and courtyards, and hosts who look after every guest personally, all 10–15 minutes from Udaipur city centre.

faqs.q: Is Devra a good boutique stay in Udaipur for couples?
faqs.a: Yes. With only eight rooms, quiet corners, a terrace with Aravalli views and sunset dinners, Devra is a favourite boutique stay in Udaipur for couples and honeymooners.

faqs.q: How far is Devra from Udaipur city centre and the airport?
faqs.a: Devra is 10–15 minutes (about a 7-minute drive) from Udaipur city centre, about 12 km from Udaipur railway station and 32 km from Maharana Pratap Airport.

faqs.q: What are the check-in and check-out times?
faqs.a: Check-in is from 1:00 pm and check-out is by 11:00 am.

faqs.q: What can Devra arrange on request?
faqs.a: Yoga, mehendi, taxis, autos (tuk-tuks), laundry and baked goods to order. A visit to the village school with the owners can also be arranged.

faqs.q: How many rooms does Devra have?
faqs.a: Devra has eight spacious, soundproof rooms: six with a double bed and two with twin beds. Some rooms also have a bay-window day bed. Every room has an attached bathroom with amenities and air conditioning.
Yes. Devra is a pet-friendly homestay in Udaipur, and pets are welcome on the open land of the estate. Please tell us about your pet when you book.

faqs.q: Does Devra have a swimming pool?
faqs.a: Yes, Devra has an infinity pool with a view of the Udaipur city line.

faqs.q: What food is served at Devra?
faqs.a: Home-cooked traditional Rajasthani food made with organic vegetables from our own farms, along with North Indian dishes. Food can be customised to your taste and dietary needs.

faqs.q: Can you arrange airport or railway station pickup?
faqs.a: Yes, pickup and drop from Udaipur airport and railway station can be arranged on prior booking. Taxis and autos (tuk-tuks) can be arranged for sightseeing.

faqs.q: Is Devra safe for solo women travellers and families?
faqs.a: Yes. Devra takes pride in being safe and friendly for solo women travellers from across the globe, and it is a favourite with families, couples and groups of friends.

faqs.q: How do I reach Udaipur from Delhi?
faqs.a: Direct flights from Delhi to Udaipur take about an hour and a half. Overnight trains such as the Mewar Express also run from Delhi, and Udaipur is roughly 660 km from Delhi by road.

faqs.q: When is the best time to visit Udaipur?
faqs.a: October to March is the most pleasant time to visit Udaipur. The monsoon months, roughly July to September, are green and the lakes fill up, which many guests love too.
